findings.description: The required all-rule composition layer does not exist. The only new implementation returns a partial role group; there is no production rule manifest, checked complete scope, independent expected-consumption inventory or conjunction with the temporal and warrant groups. All 30 conjunction tests stop at the missing-module assertion according to the supplied gate. The proposal explicitly retaining an incomplete attempt does not satisfy the sealed acceptance.

Frozen authored-content correspondence uses ordinary Python dictionary equality, which conflates distinct JSON types. In an isolated execution of the actual preparation and digest functions, a draft with sample_design.n_per_arm=true and its frozen successor with n_per_arm=1, with recomputed valid outer hashes, predecessor pin and frozen digest, produced no diagnostics and usable support. This both conceals the changed authored transition and admits the corrupt draft operand. The existing changed-protocol test does not distinguish this case.

The InstrumentRun arm-membership guard lacks its own deletion-sensitive negative control. The unknown-arm case exercises EvidenceArm, while the run/link arm mismatch uses a valid second arm and tests a different guard. Independently disabling only arm membership for InstrumentRun made a run with a nonexistent arm usable without diagnostics, while all 514 parameterized direct role-test cases still passed. The field matrix treats arm as text and cannot detect this semantic omission.

Role timing operands are stored in three group-global dictionary slots and overwritten for every link. The per-pair freeze tuple retains only hypothesis-before-freeze and membership, without the link identity or its registration/evidence/run timing results. An isolated two-evidence resolution probe returned registration_after_freeze=false and run_after_freeze=null in one submitted-evidence order, then true/true when that order was reversed, with no diagnostics in either case. A consumer cannot safely associate these exported operands with each pair.
